title: Grateful Dead Live at The Music Box on 1969-04-15
lineage: Aiwa hand-held microphone > Master Reel (Aiwa 5 inch reel-to-reel) > Alesis Masterlink 9600 > Hard Drive > CD > EAC > Samplitude Professional v7.02 > shntool > FLAC16

ai_review.summary: A raw hand‑held audience tape that still delivers a blistering 1969 show, highlighted by an epic Dark Star and soaring Turn On Your Lovelight.
ai_review.review: Despite the lo‑fi, chatty handheld mic, this recording captures one of the band’s most intense early performances. Reviewers rave about the monster Dark Star, Turn On Your Lovelight, China Cat Sunflower and The Other One, while noting that the audience ambience adds historic charm even if it sometimes intrudes. Overall the music far outweighs the modest sound quality.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars and praise the performance; recording is praised as good for an audience tape despite some chatter and fidelity limits.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hand‑held mic captures full audience ambience with occasional chatty interruptions; overall clear enough to enjoy, though low‑end mud and high‑frequency hiss are noted. Some listeners needed EQ adjustments.

standout_songs: Sitting on Top of the World
show_quality.setlist_flow: Energy stays high throughout with seamless segues—especially the legendary China Cat → The Other One transition—and a powerful second‑set climax in Dark Star and Lovelight.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals and guitar praised as front‑and‑center; his axe sounds great and drives the jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as a ‘monster’ on bass, providing a solid wall of sound and contributing to the main ten in Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned briefly (dismissively) but no detailed praise or criticism.
